question: If a person covers 90 km at a speed of 45 km/h and another distance of 150 km at a speed of 50 km/h, then his average speed for the whole journey is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Average Speed** = **Total Distance** ÷ **Total Time**

Total Distance = 90 + 150 = 240 km

Total Time = (90 ÷ 45) + (150 ÷ 50) = 2 + 3 = 5 hours

Average Speed = 240 ÷ 5 = 48 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 48 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd89e63be809bbfb91a4a741dd6080532f05635d748380a7ececa1285ccea4fb.png] 

**Given:**

Distance₁ = 90 km, Speed₁ = 45 km/h

Distance₂ = 150 km, Speed₂ = 50 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = (D₁ + D₂) ÷ (T₁ + T₂)

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken for first part (T₁) = 90 ÷ 45 = 2 hours

⇒ Time taken for second part (T₂) = 150 ÷ 50 = 3 hours

⇒ Total Distance = 90 + 150 = 240 km

⇒ Total Time = 2 + 3 = 5 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 240 ÷ 5 = 48 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 48 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distances

If two equal distances are covered at speeds u and v, the average speed is given by (2 × u × v) ÷ (u + v).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed is the difference (S₁ − S₂). In the **opposite direction**, it is the sum (S₁ + S₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.</p
